questions.subtopic: Chemical Reactions of Aldehydes and Ketones
questions.stem:
Write the major products in the following :
(i) \(\mathrm{C_6H_5CHO} \xrightarrow[273-283\ \mathrm{K}]{\mathrm{HNO_3 + H_2SO_4}}\)
(ii) \(\mathrm{C_6H_{11}COONa} + \mathrm{NaOH} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\mathrm{CaO}}\)
(iii) \(\mathrm{CH_3CHO} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{NH_2OH}}\)
questions._figure: ILLUSTRATIVE — All three reactants are printed as DRAWN STRUCTURES, not formulas. Read at 3x on page idx 6: (i) a hexagon with three Kekule double bonds bearing CHO on the top vertex, over an arrow labelled HNO3 + H2SO4 above and 273 - 283 K below; (ii) a PLAIN hexagon with no double bonds at all - i.e. SATURATED, cyclohexane, not benzene - bearing COONa, plus NaOH, over an arrow labelled CaO above and delta below; (iii) CH3 - C = O drawn two-dimensionally with H on a vertical bond below the carbonyl carbon, over an arrow labelled NH2OH. The linear LaTeX in the stem is a faithful reading of each drawing, and the aromatic-vs-saturated call on (i) versus (ii) is independently corroborated by the marking scheme's own answers: (i) gives m-nitrobenzaldehyde, so that ring is aromatic; (ii) gives CYCLOHEXANE, which only follows from decarboxylation of the sodium salt of cyclohexanecarboxylic acid, so that hexagon is saturated; (iii) gives ethanal oxime. Answerable from the stem text, hence ILLUSTRATIVE, but the crop should be attached because the page does not look like the formulas. Page idx 6.

questions.context: Amines constitute an important class of organic compounds derived by replacing one or more hydrogen atoms of ammonia molecule by alkyl/aryl groups. Amines are usually formed from nitro compounds, halides, amides, etc. They exhibit hydrogen bonding which influences their physical properties. Alkyl amines are found to be stronger bases than ammonia. In aromatic amines, electron releasing and withdrawing groups, respectively increase and decrease their basic character. Reactions of amines are governed by availability of the unshared pair of electrons on nitrogen. Influence of the number of hydrogen atoms at nitrogen atom on the type of reactions and nature of products is responsible for identification and distinction between primary, secondary and tertiary amines. Reactivity of aromatic amines can be controlled by acylation process.

questions._flag: CBSE's own marking scheme accepts TWO different orderings for this question and says why. It prints '(CH3)3N < C2H5NH2 < NH3 < C6H5NH2 / C2H5NH2 < (CH3)3N < NH3 < C6H5NH2' followed by '(As no medium (aqueous /gaseous) or phase is given both answers to be considered).' So the Board itself records the stem as under-specified. This is NOT a voided question and carries no _cbseVoided flag: the scheme does not award marks regardless of what is written, it names two specific acceptable orderings and a third would score zero. Recorded here so the ambiguity is not lost, and so whoever authors the solution gives BOTH orderings rather than silently picking one. (The 56/2/1 opener carries the identical question and the identical note.)
